overlay.why: Upstream claims design/redesign of anything; dfw routes it to its domain (critique/audit/refine).
pin creates bare /<command> shortcuts outside the plugin namespace.
`hooks on` writes hook entries into settings files; dfw provides a controlled check hook instead.

The upstream page is a full guide to `hooks on`, which writes hook entries into host settings (also ~/.claude/settings.json). dfw strips the hooks, so the page is replaced by a note that they must not be enabled.

Upstream's hooks reference says `context` restores missing hook entries when local consent exists. The shipped text does not show that IMPECCABLE_HOOK_DISABLED=1 stops that write, so the instruction is bounded in words.
`doctor --fix` can rewrite hook entries in host settings without asking; dfw forbids enabling or repairing Impeccable hooks.
Applies the approved privacy defaults to every invocation, including ones the model runs from the skill text.
Windows twin of the sh launcher defaults; after setlocal so they reach the engine process without leaking into the caller shell.
